raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Description Follow up on #8345 by applying issue-time completion recording to all asynchronous GTP weight gathers, including dense and activation-recompute gathers. Previously, grouped-expert FC1/FC2 gathers recorded completion at issuance, while other gathers recorded it at consumption. This required a `completion_recorded` flag to distinguish the two paths. This change uses one consistent policy: ```python with torch.cuda.stream(ag_stream): # Issue asynchronous gather. ... if handle is not None: handle.wait() event.record() handle = None ``` The underlying communication wait establishes the NCCL → AG-stream dependency **before** recording the event. Consumers still wait on that event before using the weights. Recording at issuance prevents unrelated later AG-stream work from extending the consumer’s dependency. ## Changes - Apply issue-time completion recording to all asynchronous weight gathers. - Remove `completion_recorded`, consume-side event recording, and the unused AG-stream cache. - Preserve host tracking, CUDA-graph handoff handling, and consumer event waits. - Leave synchronous on-demand gathers and reduce-scatter behavior unchanged. ## Validation GPU validation on four GB300 GPUs: **101 tests passed per rank**: - 15 completion-ordering and grouped CUDA-graph tests. - 80 basic GTP tests. - 3 recomputation tests. - 3 graph-gradient tests.
